5.1.intro: These days, the ad itself picks who stops to look. So having lots of different ads matters a lot.

steps.say: Open Meta Ads Manager. Click the **Ads** tab. Count how many different ad ideas are live. Resized copies don't count.
steps.check: You have a number. As a rough guide, fewer than 6 ideas means you need more ads.
steps.lost: Count your live ads with different ideas. Write the number.

steps.say: Check your main ad set for new people uses a wide audience: Advantage+ audience, or just country and age.
steps.check: Your audience is wide, and your ads do the picking.
steps.lost: Open your main ad set. Is the audience wide? Yes or no.

steps.say: Set a goal for new ads, like 4 to 8 new ads every two weeks.
steps.check: You wrote down how many new ads you'll make.
steps.lost: Write: "4 new ads every two weeks."

5.2.intro: Making ads works best as a loop. Each loop makes the next ads smarter.

steps.say: **Research** for 20 minutes: read reviews and comments, and look at other brands' ads in the Meta Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library).
steps.check: You have 3 to 5 notes.
steps.lost: Read five reviews. Write three notes.

steps.say: **Plan**: pick the topic, the reason to buy, and the one thing you'll test.
steps.check: You have a one-line test plan.
steps.lost: Write: "I'm testing ___ against ___."

steps.say: **Brief**: write one page per ad idea, using the template in Lesson 7.9.
steps.check: Each idea has a page anyone could make it from.
steps.lost: Write a short page for one idea.

steps.say: **Make** the ads: yourself, with creators, or with AI editing tools.
steps.check: You have files in 4:5 and 9:16 sizes.
steps.lost: Make one ad in two sizes: 4:5 and 9:16.

steps.say: **Launch** the new ads together on the same day.
steps.check: They all start together, so it's fair.
steps.lost: Turn on all new ads on one day.

steps.say: **Learn**: after 7 days, score each ad. Write one line on why each winner won.
steps.check: Your next brief starts from what you learned.
steps.lost: After a week, write why your best ad won.

5.3.intro: Every ad does one of four jobs: teach, prove, feel, or stand for something. Use all four.

steps.say: Label each live ad with one job: **Teach** (demos), **Prove** (reviews, results), **Feel** (fears and wishes) or **Stand for** (opinions, myth busting).
steps.check: Every ad has one label.
steps.lost: Give each ad one word: Teach, Prove, Feel or Stand for.

steps.say: For your next ad, choose what it's about: the product, the brand, the result, or the customer.
steps.check: Your next brief names one job and one focus.
steps.lost: Pick one: product, brand, result or customer.

steps.say: Make at least one ad about the customer: show them and their life after using the product.
steps.check: You have a customer ad. These often reach the most people.
steps.lost: Make one ad that shows a happy customer.

5.4.intro: What makes you different comes in layers. Each ad leads with one layer.

steps.say: Write one line each: **feature** (what it has), **benefit** (what that does for them), **proof** (why believe it), **personality** (how buying from you feels), **offer** (the deal).
steps.check: You have five lines.
steps.lost: Write one line for each of the five words.

steps.say: For your next ad, pick one layer to lead with, and one or two to back it up.
steps.check: The brief names a lead layer.
steps.careful: During a sale, lead with the offer. Other times, lead with product and proof.
steps.lost: Pick one layer to lead your next ad.

5.5.intro: Some people have never heard of you. Some are ready to buy. Each needs a different ad.

steps.say: Read the five stages in the lesson table. Label each live ad with the stage it talks to.
steps.check: Every ad has a stage.
steps.lost: For each ad: is it for strangers, or for people who know you?

steps.say: Check strangers see early-stage ads, and visitors see later-stage ads.
steps.check: Each audience gets ads made for it.
steps.lost: Strangers get intro ads. Visitors get "ready to buy" ads.

steps.say: Make one new ad for the stage you're missing most.
steps.check: Your next batch covers a missing stage.
steps.lost: Make one ad for the stage with no ads.

5.6.intro: People buy for deep reasons: belonging, status, curiosity, relief, value and more. One reason per ad.

steps.say: For each ad in your next batch, pick one reason people buy. Write it on the brief.
steps.check: Each brief names exactly one reason.
steps.lost: Pick one reason per ad.

steps.say:
Match the feeling to the moment.

1. Sale ads: show the saving and the end date.
2. Launch ads: tease what's new and who it's for.
steps.check: Sale and launch ads use different reasons.
steps.lost: Sale ad: saving + end date. That's it.

5.7.intro: The hook is the first 3 seconds. Its only job is to stop people scrolling.

steps.say: Write 3 different hooks for your next ad. Ideas: movement or a surprising first picture, calling out a group ("For runners with flat feet..."), the result first, a one-star review answered, or a curious question.
steps.check: You have 3 hooks of different types.
steps.lost: Write three different first lines.

steps.say: Make one version of the ad for each hook. Keep everything else the same.
steps.check: You have 3 ads that only differ in the first 3 seconds.
steps.lost: Same ad, three different starts.

steps.say: After 7 days, compare hook rate in Ads Manager (3-second plays ÷ impressions). It's a custom metric (Lesson 7.11).
steps.check: You know your best hook. A common rule of thumb: above about 25% is good.
steps.careful: A bold line on a still picture can work too. Test pictures as well.
steps.lost: After a week, see which start kept the most people.

5.8.intro: A script framework is a proven order for the parts of an ad. It stops rambling.

steps.say: Pick one framework from the lesson table, like "problem, make it worse, solve" or "N reasons why".
steps.check: Your brief names the framework.
steps.lost: Pick "problem, make it worse, solve".

steps.say: Fill in each part in one or two lines.
steps.check: You have a script of 20 to 45 seconds.
steps.lost: One line for each part.

steps.say: End with a clear ask: what to do ("Tap Shop now"), what they get, and why now. State the offer and any minimum ("20% off your first order, free shipping over $80").
steps.check: Your ending has all three parts.
steps.lost: End with: do this, get this, because now.

5.9.intro: During a launch or sale, the mood changes each day. Match your ads to it.

steps.say: Before launch, run teaser ads that build excitement.
steps.check: Teasers run 3 to 7 days before launch.
steps.lost: Run one teaser ad a few days before.

steps.say: On launch day, switch to excited ads. During the sale, add reviews for reassurance.
steps.check: Ads change on launch day and again mid-sale.
steps.lost: Launch day: excited ad. Mid-sale: review ad.

steps.say: In the last 24 hours, run "ends tonight" ads. Afterwards, post a thank-you.
steps.check: The last day and the day after have their own message.
steps.lost: Last day: "ends tonight". After: "thank you".

5.10.intro: Ads that look like normal posts usually do better. A phone and a real person are enough.

steps.say: Film on a phone with a real person in a real place.
steps.check: It looks like a post a friend would share.
steps.lost: Film a real person with your phone.

steps.say: Add movement in the first 3 to 5 seconds. In longer videos, change something every 1 to 2 seconds: a cut, angle, text or zoom.
steps.check: The video never sits still for long.
steps.lost: Make something move in the first few seconds.

steps.say: Add captions to every video.
steps.check: It makes sense with the sound off.
steps.lost: Turn on captions.

steps.say: Use a popular format from your feed, with your own product and your own words.
steps.check: Familiar shape, but every word and shot is yours.
steps.lost: Borrow the style, not the content.

5.11.intro: Make about 30% brand-new ideas and 70% new versions of ads that already work. Guess before you test.

steps.say: Split your next batch: about 30% new ideas, 70% new versions of winners (new hook, first picture, creator, length or captions).
steps.check: Your plan shows the split.
steps.lost: For every 10 ads: 3 new, 7 versions of winners.

steps.say: Write a guess for each ad. For example: "A review hook will beat the demo hook."
steps.check: Every new ad has a written guess.
steps.lost: Write one guess per ad.

steps.say: As spend grows, give more money to proven winners.
steps.check: Winners get most spend. New ideas get enough to be judged.
steps.careful: Don't test everything at once without knowing what you want to learn.
steps.lost: Give your best ad the most money.

5.12.intro: When it's clear who an ad is for, Meta finds those people more easily.

steps.say: For your next ad, name one group (like new mums, trail runners or home bakers). Show that kind of person using it.
steps.check: Viewers can tell in 3 seconds who it's for.
steps.lost: Pick one group. Show one of them in the ad.

steps.say: Say the group's name out loud or on screen in the first line.
steps.check: The ad talks to one group.
steps.lost: Start with: "For ___ ..."

5.13.intro: You can give people a reason to buy now without a discount. That protects your profit.

steps.say: Pick one honest reason to buy now this month: the season, an event, a limited bundle, a gift for a set time, or a delivery cut-off ("order by Friday for Christmas").
steps.check: You have one reason with a real date.
steps.lost: Pick one real date reason.

steps.say: Add it to one ad and to the top of your product pages.
steps.check: Shoppers see why to act now.
steps.lost: Put the reason on your product page.

5.14.intro: People who know you but haven't bought need answers, not more introductions.

steps.say: Make one ad for them: a comparison, reviews, an FAQ video, your guarantee, "what you get", or a creator talking about it.
steps.check: You have one ad that answers doubts.
steps.lost: Make one ad with three reviews.

steps.say: Show it to people who visited or engaged in the last 30 days.
steps.check: Warm visitors see an ad that answers their doubts.
steps.lost: Choose "visited in the last 30 days" as the audience.

5.15.intro: Good tools make ads faster and keep them looking right everywhere.

steps.say: Make picture templates in 4:5 (feed) and 9:16 (stories and reels). Keep text inside the safe zones.
steps.check: Text is never covered by buttons.
steps.lost: Make two sizes. Keep text away from the edges.

steps.say: In your phone editor, cut silences, add captions and a text hook, and export in each size.
steps.check: Each video is ready in both sizes.
steps.lost: Cut the quiet bits. Add captions. Export.

steps.say:
Let AI help.

1. Use an AI tool to resize your ad and make versions.
2. Add an AI voice-over if you want.
3. Label AI-made people and voices where the platform's rules say so.
steps.check: More versions in less time, labelled where needed.
steps.lost: Use an AI tool to resize one ad.

steps.say: Before launch, open **Advantage+ creative** in the ad and check **Enhancements** and **Advanced preview**. Turn off any you don't want.
steps.check: The ad shows exactly as you made it.
steps.lost: Check auto-enhance settings before you publish.

5.16.intro: Big brands spend a lot on seasonal moments. Watching them gives you free ideas.

steps.say: Once a month, write down 3 campaigns big brands run around a season or moment.
steps.check: You have a short list of ideas.
steps.lost: Write one big-brand idea you liked.

steps.say: Make one smaller version: a trend format, a team-up with another small brand, or a playful take.
steps.check: Your next batch has one moment-led ad.
steps.lost: Make one ad inspired by it, in your own way.

5.19.intro: A tiny true story keeps people watching. Your product is the hero.

steps.say: Pick one real moment from a customer review or your own life. It should show the problem your product fixes.
steps.check: One sentence, like "My hands cracked every winter, even with three creams."
steps.lost: Think of one time the problem annoyed someone.

steps.say: Write the story in three short lines. Line 1: the problem. Line 2: the moment things changed (finding your product). Line 3: life now.
steps.check: Three lines you can read out loud in under 20 seconds.
steps.lost: Problem. Change. Now.

steps.say: Add a "villain" if there is one. The villain is the thing that caused the problem, like cheap glue, cold wind or a confusing old way of doing things.
steps.check: The viewer knows what to be annoyed at, and your product beats it.
steps.lost: What caused the problem? That is the villain.

steps.say: Film it as one person talking to the camera, or as a voice-over on clips of the product in use. Put the problem in the first 3 seconds (Lesson 5.7).
steps.check: A 20 to 40 second video that starts with the problem.
steps.lost: Say the problem first, then show the product.

steps.say: Run it next to your normal ads for one week. Compare how long people watch (hold rate) and cost per sale (Lesson 7.11).
steps.check: You know if stories work for your product, and you make 2 more if they do.
steps.lost: Run it for a week and compare.

5.20.intro: Use popular shapes of posts, talk to one small group of fans, and make people curious.

steps.say: Spend 15 minutes scrolling TikTok or Instagram Reels. Save 5 posts that grabbed you, from any kind of account, not just stores.
steps.check: A saved folder with 5 posts that hold attention.
steps.lost: Scroll for 15 minutes and save 5 posts you liked.

steps.say: For each one, write down the format in a few words. For example: "split screen, before and after", "list of 3 mistakes" or "reacting to a comment".
steps.check: 5 formats you could copy without copying the content.
steps.lost: Name the shape of each post in a few words.

steps.say: Pick one small group of people who love your kind of product. For example: night-shift nurses, new dog owners or people who camp in winter. Write the words they use and the jokes they share.
steps.check: One group, with 5 of their own words or in-jokes.
steps.lost: Pick one group of fans and write their words.

steps.say: Make one ad that uses a saved format, speaks to that group, and opens with a question or a surprise. For example, "Nobody told me this about winter camping..." Answer it later in the video.
steps.check: One new ad that feels made for that group and makes people want to keep watching.
steps.lost: Use one shape, talk to that group, start with a question.

steps.say: Test it with your normal ads (Lesson 7.10). Keep the format if it wins, and try it with a second group next week.
steps.check: A short list of formats and groups that work for your store.
steps.lost: Test it like any other ad.

5.21.intro: Two free apps are enough to make good ads. Learn the basics once.

steps.say: Open the design app. Make a new design in the size 1080 x 1350 (for feeds). Make a second one in 1080 x 1920 (for stories and reels).
steps.check: Two blank designs in the right sizes.
steps.lost: Make two blank designs: 1080 x 1350 and 1080 x 1920.

steps.say: Add your logo, your brand colours and your fonts to the app's brand settings (Lesson 3.3).
steps.check: Every new design can use your brand look in one tap.
steps.lost: Add your logo and colours once.

steps.say: Make one still ad: one product photo, one short headline (under 8 words) and one review star line. Keep the words away from the top and bottom edges, where buttons cover them.
steps.check: A clean image ad that you can read in 2 seconds.
steps.lost: One photo, a few words, some stars.

steps.say: Open the video app. Add 3 to 5 short clips of your product. Cut any slow or silent parts.
steps.check: A video under 30 seconds with no dead moments.
steps.lost: Put in 3 to 5 clips and cut the slow bits.

steps.say: Add captions with the auto-caption tool. Then add a text hook on the first second.
steps.check: People who watch with the sound off still understand the ad.
steps.lost: Tap auto-captions, then add a first line of text.

steps.say: Export in both sizes and save each one as a template to reuse next week.
steps.check: Next week's ads take half the time.
steps.lost: Save both sizes and keep the file as a template.

5.22.intro: Ads wear out. Catch it early and swap in a fresh one.

steps.say: Open Ads Manager and show the **Frequency**, cost per purchase and click-through rate (CTR, the share of people who click) columns.
steps.check: You can see how many times, on average, each person has seen each ad.
steps.lost: Find the Frequency column under Columns > Customise.

steps.say: Write down each ad's cost per purchase and CTR for its first 7 days. This is its starting level.
steps.check: Every live ad has a starting cost per purchase and CTR noted.
steps.lost: Just note the cost per purchase for now.

steps.say: Once a week, compare each ad with its starting level. Mark it as tired when CTR has dropped by about a third and cost per purchase is clearly higher for 7 days in a row.
steps.check: You know which ads are tired, based on a week of numbers, not one bad day.
steps.lost: Look at one ad only to start.

steps.say: Check frequency for the same ads. In cold campaigns, a frequency climbing past about 3 in a week while results fall is a strong sign people have seen it enough.
steps.check: Tired ads are confirmed by both falling results and rising frequency.
steps.lost: If you can't find frequency, use falling CTR alone.

steps.say: Keep 2 to 3 new ads ready at all times, with a new hook, a new face or a new format, not just a new colour.
steps.check: You can swap in a fresh ad the same day an old one tires.
steps.lost: Start with one new hook on your best ad.

steps.say: Add the new ads next to the tired one, then turn the tired ad off once the new ones have spent about 2 times your break-even cost per purchase.
steps.check: Results recover without restarting the whole campaign.
steps.careful: Near-identical ads count as the same ad to the platform. A real refresh changes the idea, the first 3 seconds or the person on screen.
steps.lost: Turn the old ad off a week after the new one starts.
